examples.gloss: ka - InScript puts ಕ on the physical K key (K→ಕ)
examples.built: InScript is positional: every key maps to a fixed letter. ಕ sits on K; its aspirate ಖ on shift+K.

examples.gloss: kā - the ā-sign (಼a) is on E
examples.built: Consonant vowel-signs have their own keys: typing e after a consonant adds ಾ, so k + e = ಕಾ.

examples.gloss: ki - short i is on F
examples.built: k + f = ಕಿ; like ā, the short-i sign is a dedicated InScript key, not a combination.

examples.gloss: kra - & is a dedicated conjunct key
examples.built: InScript bakes the most common conjuncts into single keys (& = ಕ್ರ). Same idea as KGP's action keys.

examples.gloss: kSa - virama on d, then ಷ on ,
examples.built: Type the virama key (d) between two consonants to build any conjunct: k + d + , = ಕ್ಷ. This is the general InScript way.
ಱ (the old rra) is preserved on J in the InScript keymap, alongside modern ಙ/E, ನ, ಳ etc.

findings.title: InScript (IS 16394) - the government-standard positional layout
findings.body:
Every key maps to one fixed Kannada letter, so the mapping is positional rather than phonetic - it matches the InScript wiring in Windows/Linux and the Wikimedia jQuery.IME kn-inscript rule set this data was generated from.

Data fix applied: the upstream alternate-layer entry for key F was a malformed escape (\uC88C, which renders as a Hangul syllable); corrected to ಌ (U+0C8C VOCALIC L), matching the enhanced variant and the ISCII historic set.

findings.title: Historic and rare letters live on the Alternate (⌥/AltGr) layer
findings.body: ಌ ಽ ೄ ೞ ೠ ೡ ೢ ೣ ೱ ೲ (and ₹) are reachable by holding ⌥ (Alt) plus the shown key - the reference strip below the keyboard maps each one. ಱ is actually on the base layer at shift+J.

findings.title: Vowel signs and conjuncts are keyed, not computed
findings.body: Each vowel sign (ಿ ೀ ು ೂ ೆ ೇ ೈ ೊ ೋ ೌ) has its own physical key, and the common conjuncts (ಕ್ರ ಜ್ಞ ತ್ರ) are dedicated keys; any other conjunct is spelled via the virama key d (consonant + d + consonant).
